HealthBrowse AI · Engineering record 01

Implementation audit

Evidence reviewed 5 November 2026. Scope includes the documented MedBrowse release, the enterprise blueprint and the educational browser developed in this workspace.

BaselineAccess & rightsDesignEvidence pipelineValidation & rollout

Research briefs and evidence checks

A disease search shows a direct answer, six clinical decks and expandable research resources. Every reading mode uses a click-to-open buddy. The research companion offers general, genetics, and therapy publication searches. Up to five qualifying papers are ranked per search. Cross-checks use Europe PMC and PubMed, or PubMed and Crossref when the primary service is unavailable. Trial recruitment and completion are separately identified from ClinicalTrials.gov. Matching NIH awards are reported from RePORTER with project IDs and budget dates. These registries cover only a portion of research worldwide.

The claim checker compares a proposed passage or metadata field to an identified source record for the same topic. If a correction is uniquely supported, it may use that field instead; otherwise it withholds the claim. This process measures textual support and does not establish clinical validity or detect every form of misinformation. The source guide names ten public-health organizations and describes their scope. None is represented as certifying HealthBrowse.

Clinical decks · source coverage

The 20 focus areas from the supplied images have indexed courses, guidelines, publications, research tools, risk resources and care directories. Broader searches use the National Library of Medicine’s English MedlinePlus health topic XML feed. The feed snapshot is dated 5 November 2026. Credit: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine. An indexing descriptor is not an equivalent billing code.

GHR content is tracked through MedlinePlus Genetics. Historical NIHSeniorHealth excerpts link to pinned archive records. Additional publisher links include GARD, NIDDK, NINDS, Cancer.gov, NHLBI and CDC when the inventory has a relevant page. Course, dataset and directory listings require independent review. No resource is labeled clinically certified solely because it was reachable online.

Section-specific source ordering uses resource type, publisher, search-title overlap and reading perspective. Live literature is ranked separately by topic, study type and date. Trained neural reranking and neural architecture search are proposed experiments; the prototype has no validated model for those stages.

Clinical workspace and copilot · current release

The six clinical decks share a topic, evidence list, reading mode and active card with a source-grounded buddy. Five audience profiles select different depth, source context, learning prompts and safety guidance. Browser and buddy use the same question-answering path. The panel returns a source passage or a statement of insufficient evidence. Historical MedQuAD material is attributed alongside the excerpts. Bibliographic ranking is separate from clinical validation. The public browser has no running FLAN-T5 checkpoint or clinical deployment approval.

Only recognized condition labels leave the tab for literature and figure retrieval. Research chats can be saved to the authenticated account. Saving is on by default and can be disabled in settings; personal medical details must not be entered. Session context is also kept within the tab. A local screen intercepts recognized identifiers and emergency phrases. It has not been validated as a comprehensive de-identification or triage system.

The hosted site is public; the research desk opens after sign-in. Personal account endpoints require an authenticated Supabase user. General and Clinicians are the two self-selected reading modes after sign-in. A mode selection changes how source material is presented and grants no clinical permissions. TLS version is checked when the hosting platform exposes it. Infrastructure compliance and provider retention require independent validation.

Search and account entry

Search retrieves catalog references, ranked Europe PMC publications, and figure links extracted from open-access article XML. For uncataloged topics, it searches the supplied research keywords. These retrieval routines do not interpret medical images or generate clinical assessments. Each external service may return no matching records or a retryable failure.

Supabase handles personal account identity. The first page provides provider-managed sign-in and account creation before opening the research desk.

What the evidence establishes

Document B identifies release 820adc9. Its Appendix C names adapters, cache, gateway and reproduction scripts. The supplied workspace contained two PDFs and a screenshot, with no checkout of that release. Document A contains design targets and illustrative code fragments. Its deployment and performance claims could not be reproduced from those fragments.

1 · Documented releaseDocument B §§1–7 describes 20 sources from 11 organizations, 35 endpoint patterns, a memory/MySQL cache and source-specific expiry from 12 hours to 60 days. A curated pack spans 20 conditions and 484 unique URLs. The only bulk download reported is 33,792 US ZIP centroids. The 86 research datasets were cataloged. The reported 30 HTTP 200 responses reflect a single historical check.
2 · Source-code evidenceNo original adapters, full content pack, running database, gateway credentials or regression scripts were supplied. Document A pp. 4, 6 shows sample PubMed calls and container commands. It does not demonstrate routing, synchronization, authorization or clinical accuracy. The new browser can be inspected separately and makes no claim of continuity with the original server.
3 · Proposed workIdentity proofing, EHR access, individual clinical recommendations, native app releases, reviewed multilingual content, inventory feeds and institution-specific decision support all need independent implementation and acceptance. The new educational client has no patient record or restricted clinical endpoint.
4 · Modify and preserveRetain the seven-section order, source IDs, tier labels, typed adapters, finite caches and fallback to source text. The clinical assessment prototype was superseded by the seven-section MedCard. Use General and Clinicians reading routes while keeping permissions separate. Split government publisher authority from the quality and relevance of an individual study. Version data permissions alongside adapters.
5 · Defer costly componentsDocument A pp. 1–2, 5 proposes eight H100/A100 GPUs, 1.5 TB host RAM, Kubernetes/Cilium, distributed vectors, enterprise Neo4j and LoRA training. The corpus described in B does not establish a workload that needs them. Nor does the blueprint benchmark its sub-180 ms first-token target under representative traffic.
6 · Security & clinical gapsB §§5, 10 documents no login, raw query/feedback text, unspecified query-log retention and no licensed clinician review of the pack. Free text may identify a person even without a user ID. A p. 6 exposes a literal database password and host-published ports. Treat that credential as compromised if used, rotate it, bind databases privately and isolate ingestion from serving. Disable unrestricted logging and geolocation retention by default.
7 · Conditional accessSeparate API registration, content rights, record-level authorization, institutional agreements and professional credential verification. They answer different questions. Each integration requires its own rights record and a decision on display, caching, embedding and redistribution.
8 · No incremental service feeThe local catalog, browser filters, source links, static assets and deterministic ranking can run on already-owned hardware without paid model calls. Public metadata endpoints may allow limited keyless use. Hosting, monitoring, refreshes, clinician review, commercial licenses, devices and staff time have real costs. Public availability does not establish a production budget.
9 · Scale transitionsAdd server-side quotas, shared cache, backoff, asynchronous refresh and source health monitoring before increasing traffic. Move reviewed state to a backed-up database and replayable snapshots before adding editors or institutions. Partition tenants and regions before restricted data. Add vector search only if it improves evaluation over lexical retrieval; schedule model serving only when measured demand justifies it.

Source access and redistribution

Record owner, canonical endpoint, jurisdiction, allowed operations, attribution, limits, effective date, reviewer and next review. Default to metadata and links when rights are unknown. These are onboarding gates for a future service.

Medical literature and guidelinesB §§3, 8 identifies Europe PMC, PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov. Link to publishers and distinguish registry entries from completed studies with results. Abstracts, full texts, graphics, textbooks and videos can have separate rights. Record the resource-level license before storing or reproducing text. Require an official channel and an identifiable organization for teaching videos.
TerminologyUse versioned mappings for ICD-10-CM, MeSH, MONDO, HPO, LOINC and RxNorm. Preserve each release, attribution and license separately. ICD-11 API access requires WHO registration and keys. Verify territorial authorization before enabling SNOMED CT. Full RxNorm contains source vocabularies with additional terms. Keep OMIM bulk ingestion disabled until its provider confirms terms for the intended use. WHO access · SNOMED CT licensing · RxNorm FAQ · LOINC license
Datasets and modelsPreserve size, version, publisher, modality, intended use and restrictions per record. GEO, TCIA, GitHub, Zenodo and Hugging Face host material with varying terms. PhysioNet credentialed resources such as MIMIC-IV require user-level access controls, training and a data-use agreement. A catalog link grants no download, model-training or redistribution rights. MIMIC-IV access terms
Care and medicationPreserve official registry identity, specialty, address, location precision, verification date and registration status separately. Label map-derived results as unverified leads. Keep country-specific provenance and request location only after consent. Regulatory labels describe medicines. Stock requires a separate authorized pharmacy feed with an as-of time and stale-state policy. B §§3, 9, 10 describes US CMS/NPPES coverage, geocoding limits and a contact URL requiring correction.

Prototype and production boundary

A single responsive web client can serve browser users on desktop, iOS and Android. The prototype uses public research topics and local catalog data. It intentionally provides no clinical authorization route. Native packaging, offline update controls, mobile accessibility and a real-device compatibility matrix require a separate release.

Two reading modes

GeneralUse plain-language explanations, key facts, warning signs and cited sources. Do not provide an individual diagnosis or treatment plan.
CliniciansUse clinical terminology, diagnostic considerations, treatment evidence and source limitations. Check current guidelines, patient context and local protocols. Selecting this mode grants no access to patient records or restricted clinical actions.

Production data model

Use stable internal IDs. A specialty has an optional parent. A many-to-many disease–specialty table supports all 36 requested departments and extensions without client routing changes. Disease records hold preferred name, synonyms, classification and anatomical system. Typed edges associate symptoms, tests, guidelines, literature and genetic findings. Store terminology links as system, code, release, mapping relation, verification state and license. An exact match and a broader match must remain distinguishable.

Represent each source version with publisher, canonical URL, retrieved time, publication date, correction state and content digest where permitted. Evidence records carry DOI, PMID or NCT ID, design, population, limitations and jurisdiction. Claims reference immutable source versions and passage locators. Record score components, ranker revision, retrieval window, reviewer identity and decision. Capture original field values alongside normalized metadata. Mark unknowns explicitly.

Services and trust boundaries

Start with a read-only catalog and public metadata. The next tier is a source allowlisted API with adapter-specific timeouts, bounded retries, cached results, schema validation and a refresh queue. Keep source credentials server-side. Reject arbitrary URLs, private-network destinations, oversized responses and executable content. Retrieved text is untrusted data. Enforce read-only model tools, plain-text rendering and independently checked source IDs.

For restricted use, add OIDC identity, server-side per-action authorization, verified institution and professional status with expiry/revocation, tenant isolation, patient consent and encounter-level access. Recheck entitlement for every record request. Use managed secrets, encrypted storage and transport, restricted logs, deletion schedules, access reviews and tested restores. Scope clinical processing and third-party contracts to actual deployment jurisdiction. An architecture diagram cannot certify compliance.

From question to inspectable evidence

Proposed production workflow. Keep this separate from the prototype’s catalog search.

  1. Classify and resolve. Determine information need, entity type, audience and jurisdiction. Resolve synonyms against licensed terminology. Ambiguous abbreviations should prompt a choice. Route possible emergencies early, independent of network or model availability.
  2. Retrieve and qualify. Search approved APIs and the reviewed pack. Normalize DOI/PMID/NCT IDs, deduplicate versions and exclude retractions, unknown entities, irrelevant populations and unsuitable rights. Flag corrections and compare superseded guidance with its replacement. Preserve unavailability, unknown status and partial results.
  3. Rank by task. Prioritize topic and population match, then jurisdiction and study suitability, then freshness or current guideline status. For treatment questions prefer applicable guidelines and high-quality syntheses; for trial recruitment prefer registry status, eligibility and location. Tie-break deterministically by canonical ID. Display the decisive factors. Citation count alone must not control rank. Return at most ten qualified results.
  4. Verify the claim. Split generated sentences into atomic claims. Check that the cited passage supports subject, intervention, direction, negation, population, magnitude, units and timeframe. Independently inspect conflicts and missing applicability. A valid entity code, number match or plausible citation does not establish entailment.
  5. Recover without invention. Drop unsupported clauses. Allow one bounded rewrite against the supported passage, verify again, then show the permissible excerpt or abstain. Retain competing credible guidelines with their dates and settings. Separate publisher identity, metadata verification, clinical review and claim support in the interface.
  6. Reproduce. Export redacted normalized query, source IDs and versions, rank components, review state, software/model revisions and timestamps. Hash permitted snapshots. Replaying against a versioned fixture should reproduce the ordered result IDs. Live sources may change.

SOAP case policy

Mark subjective facts as reported and objective facts as measured. Leave missing observations unknown. Assessment must state alternatives, rationale for and against, dangerous possibilities and uncertainty. Plan headings cover investigations, treatment considerations, referral, monitoring, emergency escalation and evidence limitations. In public and student modes use educational prompts or hypothetical examples. Disable individualized recommendations until an institution approves the workflow, and retain clinician review, local protocol, contraindication and interaction checks.

Validation before extending use

Document B §7.3 reports four models correctly normalizing four queries. Its §9 reports a 20-topic coverage check. Neither measures factual entailment, patient safety, real-device usability or measured reductions in research time. The following are proposed acceptance tests, with no claimed results.

Research evaluationFreeze a dated, stratified set of guideline, rare-disease, conflicting-evidence, trial, drug and no-answer queries. Separate development and test by entity and time. Two clinical reviewers adjudicate relevance and claim support, recording disagreements. Compare lexical-only search, metadata ranking and retrieval plus generation on identical queries. Report nDCG@10, recall@10, citation precision, unsupported-claim rate, coverage versus abstention and uncertainty intervals by specialty and audience.
Clinical safetyInclude negation, changed doses/units, contradictory guidance, outdated recommendations, wrong population, missing vitals and emergency phrases. Block release for any unresolved high-severity failure, unauthorized prescription or fabricated citation in the test suite. Confirm that an upstream outage produces an explicit fallback, never a fabricated result. A passing finite suite cannot establish universal clinical accuracy.
Product and accessTest keyboard navigation, screen reader ordering, status announcements, zoom, narrow screens and tap targets on desktop, iOS Safari and Android Chrome. Compare clinician time to locate and independently verify a source against their normal workflow, while also recording correctness. Exercise revoked licenses, cross-tenant access, direct API requests, cached private data and role manipulation. Each unauthorized access attempt must fail.
Operational gatesSimulate timeouts, malformed responses, 429s, corrected articles, poisoned retrieved text, revoked rights and a failed refresh. Monitor source age, eligible-result count, refusal rate, latency percentiles, cost per query and review backlog. Alert on stale high-risk guidance. Test rollback to the last approved pack and recovery from backup. Assign a clinical owner, source steward and security owner with authority to suspend a feature.
Release sequenceFirst, public-topic research with source inspection. Second, reviewed pack plus ingestion and reproducibility with a bounded pilot. Third, institution-specific clinical evaluation in shadow mode after security and jurisdictional review. Expand clinical permissions only after signed clinical, governance and operational acceptance criteria; audit and re-evaluate after each model or source change.
